                ADDRESSING EXHIBITS TO BE ADMITTED
                   AND ORDER OF PRESENTATION


I.    EXHIBITS TO BE ADMITTED

      The parties were directed to upload the exhibits they were offering into
evidence to Kiteworks (the file-sharing platform used by the State Office of
Administrative Hearings (SOAH)) and to the Applicants’ file-sharing site
by June 3, 2026. At the prehearing conference on June 5, 2026, the Administrative

                                            1

                                  SOAH Order No. 30
                    SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
 Law Judges (ALJs) expect to admit exhibits that were uploaded into Kiteworks and
constitute either (1) direct, rebuttal, or cross-rebuttal testimony that was prefiled as
required by previous orders, subject to any rulings that have been made to objections;
and (2) discovery responses that were filed in this proceeding.


      For the parties’ reference, the ALJs have prepared Attachment A to identify
the exhibits that meet these criteria. The ALJs expect to admit the exhibits on
Attachment A at the prehearing conference unless a party identifies a material
error in the ALJs’ list. The exhibits listed on Attachment A do not include:
      • Exhibits designated as demonstrative;

      • Exhibits that a party designated for purposes of cross-examination;

      • Exhibits that were uploaded to Kiteworks that were not part of the prefiled
        direct testimony filed by that party or are not a discovery response; or

      • Exhibits with other procedural irregularities.


      To the extent that time allows, the ALJs will address issues concerning the
parties’ remaining exhibits at the prehearing conference. Otherwise, admissibility of
exhibits will be addressed during the hearing.




                                              2

                                    SOAH Order No. 30
                      SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349, PUC Docket No. 59475
 II.        ORDER OF CROSS-EXAMINATION                                 AND       PRESENTATION                OF
           INTERVENORS’ DIRECT CASES

           On June 3, 2026, Applicants filed a proposed order of presentation and
cross-examination.1 In response to filings, some corrections were made as
appropriate. While the links may have been updated in the list, the numbering and
presentation order remain the same, to avoid confusion. The ALJs’ Intervenor Order
of Presentation is attached as Attachment B.


           With one exception,2 Applicants plan to present their witnesses in a panel
format (i.e., with multiple witnesses available for cross-examination at the same
time). Applicants have proposed two separate panels: (1) a panel on the issue of need
for the Project, comprising witnesses Jared Gurley, P.E. and Collin M. Martin, P.E.;
and (2) a panel on the issue of routing for the Project, comprising witnesses
Casey D. Petty, Russell Marusak, Corin E. Cooley, P.E., KayLynne Phillips,
Kelly Wells, and Dave Elliott. At the prehearing conference on June 5, 2026, the
ALJs plan to discuss whether these witnesses should instead be presented as one
panel.


           In either case, the hearing on the merits will begin with cross-examination of
Applicants’ panel(s). Cross-examination shall proceed in the order set forth in
Attachment B. Parties are advised that:

       • An attorney or representative shall have one opportunity to cross-examine
        a panel of witnesses, regardless of the number of intervenors represented
        by that attorney.

      • If a witness has not been identified for cross-examination and their exhibits
        have been admitted, the witness will not testify at the hearing.


      Intervenors’ direct cases shall also proceed in the order indicated in
Attachment B. Errors or omissions contained in Attachment B may be addressed at
the prehearing conference, as time allows. Given the large size and expedited nature
of this proceeding, witness availability throughout all five hearing days is paramount.
The ALJs note that several parties have indicated that certain witnesses may not be
available for the entirety of the hearing. While the parties may raise such concerns as
they arise, the ALJs may be unable to accommodate all witness scheduling requests.
